newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Lennar spinoff has loan muscle.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Lennar spinoff has loan muscle.

text.p: Lennar Corp's spinoff of its fast-growing finance businesses will create a seasoned competitor able to borrow as much as $2 billion to expand, Lennar chief executive Stuart Miller said on Wednesday.
Miller told Reuters that LPC Inc, which will contain Lennar's mortgage-securities, commercial real estate and other businesses, has about $500 million in equity and some $850 million in assets.
"It has a very strong balance sheet," Miller said. "Our bankers tell us we could borrow up to $2 billion more."

Miller said the spinoff, and a simultaneous stock acquisition of fellow homebuilder Pacific Greystone Corp, will make Lennar much easier for Wall Street investors to understand and allow LPC to move more aggressively in finance markets.

Analyst Timothy Jones of Southeast Research said many institutional investors never fully valued the huge profits Lennar made from securities and real estate bought in the early 1990s, during commercial real estate and thrift crises.
"For years, the Street was not giving them value for their finance properties," Smith said.

Miller said he will be chairman of LPC and continue as chief executive of Lennar, which will become a very strong presence among big home builders in California, Texas, Arizona and Nevada. The company is already a leader in Florida, like the others one of the hottest U.S. markets for new homes.

The combination, he said, will leave Lennar shareholders with 68 percent of the new homebuilding company and stock very useful for making future acquistions. "Stay tuned," Miller said when asked if any deals were imminent.

Miller said the combination would make Lennar a healthier company with strong purchasing and borrowing advantages. He told analysts during a telephone conference call the combination would immediately add to share profits.
He declined to discuss earnings forecasts.
"The combination with Greystone sets up a very well organized, very diversified company," he said.
The acquisition gives Lennar almost 14,000 building slots in California, a huge market for new houses which is just coming out of a long slump.
"I don't believe we are at the top of a cycle in California. We are in a comfortable zone," he said.
Lennar shares shot up 4-1/4 to 30-5/8, a 52-week peak. Greystone shares were off 1-7/8 to 15-1/4.
